label: prf:reeb-operations-per-planck
title: Proof of reeb operations per planck
html:
Proof. Proof of reeb operations per planck

Proof. The Reeb time coordinate is defined as t = \hbar_q \cdot \mathcal{T} (information-theoretic time). Consequently, each discrete f_q-iteration (an increment of \mathcal{T} by 1) corresponds to a continuous time duration of \hbar_q. The number of iterations composing one full Reeb circuit (continuous duration 1) is therefore exactly 1/\hbar_q = t_P(q). \square

Regime values.

q n_R Interpretation
\to \infty \to 1 Deep-quantum: one iteration per circuit, fully discrete
q_0 \approx 10.1 Our universe (local substrate q): \sim 10 iterations per circuit
2 2 Two iterations per circuit
1.01 101 Near-classical: \sim 100 iterations per circuit
\to 1 \to \infty Classical limit: infinitely many, continuous Reeb flow

Information rate. The information processed per Planck unit is

  I_P(q) =  n_R(q) \cdot \eta_q.

Here \eta_q = (2q-1)/q^3 is the operational entropy (operational entropy). This parameter quantifies the information generated per f_q-iteration, dictated strictly by the gravitational self-consistency condition.

In the deep-quantum regime (q \to \infty), n_R \to 1 and \eta_q \to 0. The dynamics simplify entirely, yielding I_P \to 0. At the classical limit (q \to 1), \eta_q \to 1 nat per step. At q = q_0, I_P \approx 10.1 \times 0.892 \approx 9.0 q-bits per Planck time.
